title: Isle of Quel'Danas
body: The Isle of Quel'Danas rises from the sea north of Eversong Woods, and on its plateau lies the Sunwell, the fount of power that Dath'Remar Sunstrider's people kindled with water carried from the Well of Eternity. In the Third War Arthas marched the Scourge across the isle and used the Sunwell to raise Kel'Thuzad, and the defiled well was lost to the elves. Then Prince Kael'thas returned, sworn to the Burning Legion. His Dawnblade and Sunblade, with demons, naga and the Wretched, overran the island while he worked to rekindle the Sunwell as a gateway for Kil'jaeden. Against him the Aldor and the Scryers of Shattrath set aside their feud and landed as the Shattered Sun Offensive, setting out from their staging area to win back Sun's Reach piece by piece. Kael'thas fell in his Magisters' Terrace, the Deceiver was turned back, and the Sunwell now burns pure under the guard of Halduron Brightwing's wardens. Yet the Offensive fights on for Sun's Reach, while demons and Scourge clash along the Dead Scar and naga hold the Greengill Coast.

title: Shattered Sun Staging Area
body: The Shattered Sun Staging Area is where the Offensive musters newcomers before sending them into the fight. Exarch Larethor, a draenei, commands here beside Captain Theris Dawnhearth, a blood elf who directs the effort to win back Sun's Reach. Drill Sergeant Bahduum greets each new draft with blunt speeches: draenei who once stood with him at Skettis and in Shadowmoon Valley hear that the situation on Azeroth looks grim, and sin'dorei used to Scryer ways are told to pull their weight or get back on the boat. Vindicator Xayann fits the island's malfunctioning sentries with new crystal cores to turn them into allies, and the quartermaster Eldara Dawnrunner keeps powerful gear for those who have proven themselves.

title: Sun's Reach Sanctum
body: The Sun's Reach Sanctum is the Offensive's first goal in the town. Wretched overran it after stealing the power sources from its protective crystal wards, so winning it back means feeding the wards with recovered mana remnants and turning the island's malfunctioning sentries into allies for the assault. Once it is secure, its energy is to open a portal from Shattrath, kept alive by mana cells seized from ethereal smugglers in Outland. From the sanctum Battlemage Arynna and Harbinger Inuuro plan the push on the armory, and Astromancer Darnarian grumbles over his translocations. In time a Monument to the Fallen rises beside it, raised from donations to honor those who died retaking Sun's Reach.

title: Sun's Reach Armory
body: The Sun's Reach Armory is held by the Burning Legion when the Offensive turns on it. Harbinger Inuuro sends fighters to break the demons' morale by slaying the emissaries of hate they rally around and impaling them on Shattered Sun banners, while dragonhawk raids keep the Legion's forces busy on the Dead Scar. Once the armory falls, the demons are pushed back to the Dawning Square. Smith Hauthaa then raises an anvil and forge behind it to arm the Offensive, Magister Ilastar and Vindicator Kaalan plan the war against the Dawnblade from its grounds, and a group of purveyors sells exotic gear to the Offensive's champions.

title: Sun's Reach Harbor
body: Sun's Reach Harbor, the last stronghold the Offensive needs to make the town its own, is held by the Dawnblade, among the most elite of Kael'thas's armies. When it falls, a ship at the docks, Silvermoon's Pride, is taken as a prize, though it is not yet seaworthy, and Captain Valindria keeps her post aboard while she harries the naga of Greengill Coast. Archmage Ne'thul follows the assault on the Sunwell's gates from the waterfront, and Ayren Cloudbreaker keeps the Offensive's dragonhawks on the western docks. In the inn, the alchemist Mar'nah distills bloodberries, a common nuisance plant made potent by the Sunwell's power. When the victory in Sun's Reach is complete, the naaru K'iru comes to bless it.

title: The Dawnblade Fleet
body: Off the coast of Sun's Reach ride three Dawnblade warships, the Dawnchaser, the Sin'loren and the Bloodoath, crowded with reservists. They sail first to reinforce Kael'thas's hold on the harbor, and once the harbor falls they come to win it back. The Offensive meets them from the air, flying low enough over the ships to set their sails ablaze with flaming oil and then dropping onto the decks while the crews struggle with the fire. Every burned sail, Vindicator Kaalan reckons, means a long wait before the enemy can bring reinforcements again.

title: Dawnstar Village
body: Dawnstar Village lies west of the Sun's Reach Armory, a blood elf village that became the stronghold of the Dawnblade on Quel'Danas. Their summoners, blood knights and marksmen fill its lanes, practicing at archery targets and training dummies, their chargers are kept close by, and Wretched prowl the outskirts. Once driven from the harbor, the Dawnblade survivors fall back here, and Magister Ilastar wants every one of them slain, for they sealed their fate when they followed Kael'thas to the isle. At the village's edge stands the Bloodcrystal, one of the points on the island's ley lines that Astromancer Darnarian studies.

title: The Dawning Square
body: South of the Sun's Reach Sanctum, the Dawning Square belongs to the Burning Legion. A fel portal stands in the middle of the square, joined to the gateway in Outland through which Kael'thas's armies retreated to the Sunwell, and demons guard it in force: irespeakers, unleashed hellions and abyssal flamewalkers, rallied by emissaries of hate whom they fear more than any foe. It is here the Legion falls back once the Sun's Reach Armory is lost, and here the Offensive keeps up the pressure. A magistrix sent to investigate the portal never returned. Astromancer Darnarian counts it among the ley points his crystals must touch.

title: Greengill Coast
body: Greengill Coast, on the eastern shore southeast of Sun's Reach, was home to a village of Greengill murlocs until the Darkspine naga came. Their sirens now bind the murlocs with controlling orbs and set them to digging iron ore, which the naga lock in chests for shipment to the Legion. On a ley line near the shore, they have raised a shrine to Queen Azshara. The Offensive harries them carefully. Captain Valindria has the sirens' orbs smashed among the slaves so the freed murlocs turn on their masters, but only a little each day, lest the naga turn their full attention on Sun's Reach, and Smith Hauthaa wants their ore for her anvil.

title: The Dead Scar of Quel'Danas
body: The Dead Scar does not end at Silvermoon. On the isle it climbs from the southern shore toward the Sunwell Plateau, and its blight still stirs the dead: skeletal ravagers and frenzied ghouls wander it in great numbers. The Burning Legion has claimed the same ground, with wrath enforcers, eredar sorcerers and pit overlords, and the two hosts are locked in a struggle that keeps the demons too busy to fall upon the Offensive, a fight the Offensive is glad to feed from the air. At the Scar's southern end lie the remains of Thalorien Dawnseeker, who fell here holding the road to the Sunwell against the Scourge.

title: Exarch Larethor
body: Exarch Larethor, a draenei, commands the Shattered Sun Staging Area. Every soldier Shattrath can spare reports to him, Aldor sent by Adyen the Lightwarden and Scryers sent by Dathris Sunstriker, and he greets them all with the same plain warning: whatever the old feud between the two orders, neither has the strength to go it alone, so they will work together, though he has a habit of calling the Scryers cryers. Larethor kept a spy, the blood elf Tyrith, inside the Magisters' Terrace, and when Tyrith stopped reporting, the exarch sent help up the rise to find him. It came too late to save Tyrith, but not too late to make his death count.

title: Captain Theris Dawnhearth
body: Captain Theris Dawnhearth, a blood elf of the Shattered Sun Offensive, directs the campaign to retake Sun's Reach from the staging area. He began with the sanctum, sending fighters after the Wretched to recover the mana remnants they had stolen from its crystal wards, and when it fell he called for word to be sent back to Shattrath that the Offensive was making its move. Afterwards he wanted wards raised around every other building as well. When Magistrix Seyla vanished while investigating the fel portal at Dawning Square, he sent help after her with a captured Legion scroll. And when Sun's Reach was wholly won, it was Theris who proclaimed that the naaru blessed them with their presence.

title: Archmage Ne'thul
body: Archmage Ne'thul, a blood elf of the Shattered Sun Offensive, follows the struggle to break the barriers around the Sunwell from the waterfront at Sun's Reach Harbor. Despite every effort, Kael'thas's sinister work was done: the Sunwell was rekindled in readiness for the Deceiver's arrival, and three mighty gates, Agamath, Rohendor and Archonisus, held the Offensive back from its inner chambers while the Shattered Sun's mages worked to bring them down one by one. Ne'thul warns all who will listen that if Kil'jaeden rises through the Sunwell, the world will be thrown into a war the like of which it has not seen for ten thousand years.

title: Thalorien Dawnseeker
body: Thalorien Dawnseeker was a high elf warrior and the bearer of Quel'Delar, a sword given to his people long ago, which he carried against the Amani in the Troll Wars. When the Scourge came for the Sunwell, he stood among its defenders. On the Isle of Quel'Danas he ordered his soldiers back to the Sunwell to prepare its defenses and stayed behind to buy them time, swearing that none of the Scourge would reach the well while he stood. He fell to the death knight Morlen Coldgrip on the ground now called the Dead Scar, and his remains still lie at its southern end. His sword passed to Lana'thel, who carried it to Northrend.

title: Magister Ilastar
body: Magister Ilastar plans the Offensive's war against the Dawnblade from the Sun's Reach Armory. To him the Dawnblade are Kael's lackeys and dogs, and he promised to teach them a lesson in humility, sending fighters against their summoners, blood knights and marksmen until the harbor fell. Victory did not soften him. With Sun's Reach won, he admitted he was not satisfied, and sent the hunt on to Dawnstar Village after the survivors, who sealed their fate when they followed Kael'thas to the isle. He likes to wonder aloud what the prince feels as his armies fall, despair, helplessness or fear, and hopes it is all of them.

title: Smith Hauthaa
body: Smith Hauthaa refused to wait for supplies that might never arrive. Behind the Sun's Reach Armory she set out to build an anvil and forge to arm and armor the Offensive, and she found her iron among the enemy: the Darkspine naga of Greengill Coast were filling chests with ore bound for the Legion, and taking it hurt them as much as it helped her. With the anvil finished, she blends the naga ore into a special alloy with metal from corrupted armaments that fel orcs forged at the Ata'mal Terrace in Shadowmoon Valley, a place holy to the draenei. The anchorites have blessed her anvil so that it can cleanse them.

title: Astromancer Darnarian
body: Astromancer Darnarian works the translocation magic of the Sun's Reach Sanctum and feels badly underappreciated for it. Everyone, he complains, wants instant gratification and never thinks of the effort behind even the simplest portal. His remedy is education. He hands visitors a crystal and sends them to attune it to the ley lines of Quel'Danas at three points: the Bloodcrystal near Dawnstar Village, the Legion's portal in the Dawning Square, and the naga shrine on Greengill Coast. Only after checking their readings does he trust them with a translocator, warning that if a reading is faulty there is no telling where they will end up, and the blame will be theirs.

title: Anchorite Ayuri
body: Anchorite Ayuri will not let the dead of Sun's Reach be forgotten. Once the town was won, with final victory at hand, she gathered donations for a monument to those who gave their lives retaking the town, with whatever remained promised to the widows and orphans of the fallen. The Monument to the Fallen now stands in Sun's Reach, and she still collects for the families, reminding visitors of the price of every war, even one that is won. Her fellow anchorite Kairthos admits the donations have fallen short of her hopes, and quietly invites the wealthiest champions to make up the difference, promising that all who fought here will know of their deeds.

title: The Call to Quel'Danas
body: In Shattrath, the two rival orders serving the naaru received the same urgent summons. On the Aldor Rise, Adyen the Lightwarden admitted that his forces were spread thin and that a contingent had already gone to Azeroth to investigate events at the Sunwell Plateau, and he sent whomever he could spare to report to Larethor, wishing he could send more. On the Scryer's Tier, Dathris Sunstriker ordered every able hand back to Azeroth at once, to fight beside the Aldor of all people. On the isle, Drill Sergeant Bahduum laid out the stakes. Kael'thas, thought dead, had overrun Quel'Danas and was working on the plateau to reignite the Sunwell and open a rift for Kil'jaeden. If he succeeded, this world would suffer far worse than Outland ever had. Many of them would not be going home, the sergeant warned, but those who kept their wits would have the better chance.

title: The Reclamation of Sun's Reach
body: The Offensive lacked the numbers to storm Sun's Reach outright, so it took the town one piece at a time. First came the sanctum: fighters hunted the Wretched for the mana remnants stolen from its crystal wards, while Vindicator Xayann fitted new cores into the island's malfunctioning sentries and turned them into guards. With the sanctum won, its energy, fed by mana cells seized from ethereal smugglers in Blade's Edge, opened a portal from Shattrath. Next the armory, held by the Legion: emissaries of hate were slain and impaled on Shattered Sun banners while dragonhawk raids kept the demons busy on the Dead Scar, until the Legion fell back to the Dawning Square. Last came the harbor, where Magister Ilastar's fighters broke the Dawnblade. With Sun's Reach wholly taken, the naaru K'iru came to bless the victors, and a monument rose to the fallen.

title: Fire from the Sky
body: Sun's Reach was won from the air as much as on the ground. When the Offensive moved on the armory, Battlemage Arynna knew the Legion would turn on them as soon as its host to the south was free of the Scourge at the Dead Scar. Her answer was to keep it busy: riders on Ayren Cloudbreaker's dragonhawks flew over the Scar hurling arcane charges at pit overlords, eredar sorcerers and wrath enforcers, and the raids went so well that they never stopped. When a fleet of Dawnblade reservists sailed to reinforce the harbor, and later to retake it, Vindicator Kaalan sent the same riders low over the ships with flaming oil to set their sails alight, then had them drop to the decks to finish the reservists. Ayren, for one, welcomes the change from quiet postings far from the fighting.

title: The Missing Magistrix
body: Magistrix Seyla was sent to investigate the fel portal in the middle of the Dawning Square, and she never came back. Captain Theris Dawnhearth had a scroll taken from an enemy corpse that he believed would open the way, and sent help through after her. The portal led far from Quel'Danas, to the gateway at the Throne of Kil'jaeden in Outland, by which Kael'thas's armies had retreated to the Sunwell. Seyla was alive, keeping out of the Legion's sight, and had little time for Theris's worry: there were much bigger problems there. Some of Kael's most loyal followers had stayed behind and gorged on the blood of demons for days, gaining new powers, and Legion reinforcements for Quel'Danas still poured through the gateway. Seyla set out to strip the felbloods of their stolen strength and to blast the gateway itself, though she expected the demons would simply repair it.

title: Thalorien's Blessing
body: Long after Thalorien Dawnseeker fell, his defiled sword Quel'Delar was found and reforged in Northrend by a champion working with the Silver Covenant or the Sunreavers. Warned by the spirit of Uther that the blade could not be trusted while the Lich King's evil clung to it, the bearer brought it to Quel'Danas to be cleansed in the Sunwell. Ranger-General Halduron Brightwing would not admit a stranger to his people's most sacred place on a tale alone, and set a test: seek the blessing of Thalorien's remains at the southern end of the Dead Scar. There the spirit relived his last stand, sending his soldiers back to the Sunwell and calling on the stranger to fight beside him against the Scourge and the death knight Morlen Coldgrip. When the battle ended, Thalorien saw Quel'Delar, declared that it had chosen a new wielder, and gave his blessing. Halduron, his doubts answered, opened the way to the Sunwell, where the leaders of Silvermoon waited.
